claims.text: CAL FIRE's incident page for the Plaskett Fire reports that, as of September 11, 2026 at 6:31 PM, the fire (which started August 26, 2026 at 11:01 AM near Los Burros Road/Plaskett in the Los Padres National Forest, Monterey County) had burned 29,942 acres and was 83% contained, up from 79% contained the previous day; two evacuation zones have been downgraded from orders to warnings, though multiple evacuation order and warning zones remain in effect across Monterey County, and Highway 1 remains partially closed between mile marker 19 and mile marker 11.1.

CAL FIRE's incident page for the Timber Fire reports that, as of September 11, 2026 at 6:31 PM, the fire (which started August 8, 2026 at 8:35 PM southeast of Loma Vista in the Los Padres National Forest, Monterey County) had burned 25,420 acres and was 27% contained; evacuation orders have been downgraded in portions of Big Sur and previous shelter-in-place orders have been lifted as conditions improved, though 13 areas remain under evacuation orders and 27 under evacuation warnings across Monterey County, with crews conducting suppression, mop-up and patrol operations; no injuries or deaths were reported.

CAL FIRE's incident page for the Timber Fire reports that, as of September 12, 2026 at 8:02 PM, the fire had burned 25,426 acres and was 39% contained, up from 27% contained the previous day; the fire 'remains active with isolated heat in the interior and difficult-to-access portions of the fire,' with crews continuing direct suppression and mop-up operations in steep terrain, particularly in the Ventana Wilderness area.

CAL FIRE's incident page for the Plaskett Fire reports that, as of September 14, 2026 at 7:18 PM, the fire had burned 29,976 acres and was 89% contained, up from 83% contained on September 11; Evacuation Orders remain in effect for zones FHL-G011, FHL-G012-B, FHL-G014, FHL-G017, FHL-G018 and FHL-G023, while Evacuation Warnings are in effect for zones MRY-G016, MRY-F033, MRY-F034, MRY-F035 and MRY-F036, in Monterey County on Los Padres National Forest land under USFS jurisdiction, managed by California Interagency Incident Management Team 7.

description: The Plaskett and Timber wildfires have burned roughly 55,400 combined acres along California's Big Sur coast since August 2026, forcing evacuations across two counties. The Timber Fire ignited August 8 and the larger Plaskett Fire ignited August 26 in the Los Padres National Forest near Big Sur; both remain active, with CAL FIRE reporting the Plaskett Fire at about 30,000 acres and 89% contained and the Timber Fire at about 25,400 acres and 39% contained as of September 14. Evacuation orders have been downgraded in portions of Big Sur, though numerous evacuation order and warning zones remain in effect across Monterey County and a stretch of Highway 1 through the Big Sur coast remains partially closed. No deaths or injuries have been reported by CAL FIRE for either fire.

impact.summary: CAL FIRE reports no deaths or injuries from either fire. As of September 14, 2026, the Plaskett Fire's containment has risen to 89% (from 83%) on 29,976 acres, while the Timber Fire holds at 39% containment on 25,426 acres, with crews continuing suppression and mop-up in steep, difficult-to-access terrain including the Ventana Wilderness. Evacuation orders remain in effect for several zones in Monterey County for the Plaskett Fire, with additional zones downgraded to warnings, while the Timber Fire still has 13 areas under evacuation orders and 27 under warnings. A long stretch of Highway 1 through the Big Sur coast remains partially closed to through traffic.
